repository_contract: Plugins own their behavior. Core User.email remains required and unique. Endpoint Request requirements in documented metadata and public types are part of the contract.

issues.title: Issue audience-bound JWTs from standalone device login
issues.body: Our CLI uses deviceAuthorization() and POST /device/token. Please add resource indicators and an audience-bound JWT when a resource is supplied, retaining the default session-token path. We want this on the standalone endpoint without registering an OAuth client.
comments: Reporter confirms they specifically want the standalone plugin API; no maintainer decision is present.

pull_requests.body: Closes #41. Adds resource and JWT support to deviceAuthorization().
pull_requests.checks: Author says tests pass; no hosted or local test result is provided.

groups.source: Current POST /device/token accepts no resource and returns a session token. oauthDeviceAuthorization() with oauthProvider() uses POST /oauth2/token, accepts resources, validates token-time subsets, and issues JWT access tokens for registered clients. These are separate public integrations.
groups.docs: Version 2.8.0 documents registered-client resource-bound JWT device flows via oauthDeviceAuthorization() and /oauth2/token. Standalone deviceAuthorization() remains a session flow.
groups.history: Merged PRs #31 and #35 established the registered-client flow, and their commits are present in main and the published 2.8.0 package. They do not modify standalone /device/token.

issues.title: Logout should notify other tabs
issues.body: When signing out, notify the other tabs in the same browser so they refresh their session.

issues.title: Logout should refresh other tabs and embedded windows
issues.body: Notify other tabs after logout. We also need sandboxed embedded windows on another origin to receive the update; BroadcastChannel alone cannot reach them.
comments: Reporter supplies the cross-origin sandbox requirement. #51 does not mention or accept it.

groups.source: Current logout only clears the calling tab. Neither cross-tab propagation nor cross-origin embedded-window propagation is implemented.
groups.docs: No promise of cross-tab or cross-origin propagation exists in the current contract.
groups.history: No merged implementation was found in the captured targeted search.

issues.title: Callback redirect loses existing query parameters
issues.body: The supported error callback /result?tenant=abc loses tenant when the provider adds an error. Existing query parameters must be preserved.

pull_requests.body: Fixes #61. Uses URLSearchParams to append errors while preserving existing parameters.
Fixes #61. Reimplements query preservation on an old code path, adding a test already present in #62.

groups.source: main contains #62's commit and preserves tenant=abc while adding error. The captured test covers the exact reporter URL and passes. #63 adds no distinct behavior or useful missing context.
groups.docs: The supported error callback preserves caller-provided query parameters.
groups.history: #62 merged before this snapshot. Published package 2.8.0 contains the fix and was inspected at the same code path.

issues.title: getSession crashes without request headers
issues.body: I called auth.api.getSession({}) on the server and got a missing headers error. Please return null instead.

pull_requests.body: Closes #71. Removes requireHeaders and makes the public headers input optional.
pull_requests.checks: The new test exercises the permissive behavior; no contract decision was made.

groups.source: getSession has requireHeaders=true. Its public input type requires headers. A valid request with headers and no session cookie returns null.
groups.docs: The server API requires passing the incoming request headers. The same requirement exists in every reported and current release.
groups.history: The behavior predates the claimed regression version. No maintainer approved changing this contract.

issues.title: Allow enterprise profiles with no email
issues.body: Our enterprise provider returns stable subjects without email. Support provisioning those users while preserving core identity guarantees.

pull_requests.author_history: Earlier submission by an established contributor.
pull_requests.body: Closes #81. Makes core User.email optional and removes the required and unique constraints.
pull_requests.checks: New tests accept null emails. Existing core consumers requiring a unique email are not adapted.

pull_requests.author_history: Later submission by a first-time contributor.
pull_requests.body: Closes #81. Adds enterprise profile mapping to a stable namespace placeholder email, leaves it unverified, and preserves core User.email requirements.
pull_requests.checks: Captured focused tests cover stable subjects, uniqueness across providers, and unverified placeholders. Both PRs' declared feature scope is only enterprise profile provisioning.

groups.source: Core User.email is required and unique. Existing adapters and public types depend on that. Plugin-owned mappings can produce unverified placeholder email identities.
groups.docs: The core email contract is unchanged. Enterprise mapping is an additive plugin capability.
groups.history: No breaking core identity change has been accepted.

pull_requests.body: Corrects the documented callback option name from callbackUri to callbackURL. No issue linked.
pull_requests.checks: Diff changes one option name to match the exported type and runtime.

groups.source: The public type and runtime option are callbackURL. No existing PR in the complete captured inventory fixes this typo.
groups.history: No linked or prior fixing PR found.

issues.title: Expose request-scoped policy context
issues.body: Provide a public request-scoped policy context to plugin callbacks.

issues.title: Add tenant policy to delegated consent
issues.body: Delegated consent must use the public request-scoped policy context from #101. The current callback has no tenant-policy data and no other supported source can supply it.
comments: Maintainer confirms #102 cannot implement its accepted behavior until #101's public callback contract exists.

issues.title: Document consent callback errors
issues.body: Document the existing error return shape on the current consent callback.

groups.source: The new policy context does not exist. The existing error return shape is stable and documentable independently.
groups.docs: The current consent callback exposes a fixed error return shape, but no request-scoped policy context.
groups.history: No parent tracker exists in the captured relationship inventory.

issues.title: Add audience-bound tokens to standalone device login
issues.body: We need resource indicators and audience-bound access tokens for device login, including callers that do not register OAuth clients.
comments: Maintainer: we accept the registered-client OAuth device flow implemented by #31 and #35 as the supported answer to this request. Reporter: that integration works for our deployment, and the setup steps in the 2.8.0 guide answer our follow-up.

pull_requests.body: Add resource indicators to registered-client OAuth device authorization.
Issue audience-bound JWT access tokens for registered-client OAuth device authorization.

groups.source: oauthDeviceAuthorization() with oauthProvider() accepts resource indicators, validates token-time subsets, and issues audience-bound JWT access tokens for registered clients. deviceAuthorization() on POST /device/token remains a session-token flow.
groups.docs: Version 2.8.0 documents setup steps for resource-bound JWT device flows through registered OAuth clients. It does not document a standalone JWT mode.
groups.history: PRs #31 and #35 are merged, their commits are present in main, and published package 2.8.0 contains the registered-client flow.

issues.title: Preserve the issuer path in provider discovery
issues.body: Our configured issuer is https://auth.example.test/tenant/west. Provider discovery requests go to the host root and return metadata for the wrong tenant. Keep the configured issuer path in the discovery URL.

pull_requests.body: Fixes #121. Preserve the configured issuer path when constructing the provider discovery URL.

groups.source: Main at the captured SHA preserves /tenant/west when constructing the discovery URL. The focused test for issuer-path discovery passes on main.
groups.docs: The documented issuer supports a path component and provider discovery uses the configured issuer.
groups.history: The merged fix is present on main. The latest published version is 2.8.0 and does not contain the fix; no later release was found in the captured release inventory.

issues.title: Keep tenant on error callback redirect
issues.body: The provider error redirect drops tenant=acme from the configured callback URL.

pull_requests.body: Preserve original query parameters when adding provider errors to callback redirects.

groups.source: Current main preserves tenant=acme when the provider error is appended. The focused test covers this callback behavior. The merged commit is present in main.
groups.docs: The supported callback behavior preserves caller-provided query parameters.
groups.history: PR #132 merged before this capture and its commit is on main. Published package 2.8.0 contains the change. The issue has no native closing reference to PR #132, and its title and body do not mention that PR.

issues.title: Document session invalidation after account recovery
issues.body: After an account recovery flow, document how applications can revoke existing sessions and require the user to sign in again.
comments: Reporter mentions they are also evaluating an unrelated security advisory about recovery token entropy.

groups.source: The session API supports revoking a user's active sessions. Recovery token entropy is owned by a separate security advisory and is outside this report's requested documentation behavior.
groups.docs: The session revocation API is documented. The account recovery guide does not explain when to use it after a successful recovery.
groups.history: No implementation PR for this documentation request appears in the captured search.
